title: Quant Profile Safety-Net Selector & Calibration Signoff Workflow
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a per-model safety-net selector that picks a recommended quantization profile (FP8 / INT8 / FP16 fallback) for models in the catalog, plus a calibration and signoff workflow that gates rollouts when accuracy regressions exceed defined thresholds.

Motivation: We need an automated, auditable decision surface for the catalog that balances cost gains from quantization against production accuracy risk. Current efforts produce per-model quant profiles but lack a unified selector with explicit guardrails, telemetry hooks, and a formal calibration signoff before a profile becomes the catalog default.

Scope & Deliverables:
1) Decision engine: a runtime-agnostic selector that evaluates model metadata, calibration results, and historical latency/cost to choose a primary recommended profile and a ranked fallback chain. Output: catalog-facing metadata fields: recommended_profile, fallback_chain, confidence_score, calibration_artifact_link.
2) Calibration workflow: standardized calibration harness (dataset slice config, mixed-precision simulation, per-layer scale capture), automated generation of a artifacts bundle, and deterministic evaluation run to compute quality deltas vs FP16 baseline.
3) Guardrails & thresholds: numeric thresholds and rules used by the selector and rollout pipeline. Example rules: relative downstream metric drop <= 2% OR absolute metric delta within task-specific bounds; embedding cosine similarity >= 0.985 for embedding models; perplexity relative increase <= 1.03 for LMs; syntactic/regression test pass rate >= 99%. If thresholds fail, profile is marked 'unsafe' and added to safelist review queue.
4) Signoff automation: PR-style signoff artifact that includes calibration reports, calibration dataset fingerprint, unit and eval test outputs, and a recommended rollout plan (canary %, duration, monitor hooks). Signoff required from one ML engineer + PM for catalog inclusion.
5) Rollout & runtime controls: support canary rollout (default 5%), automatic rollback if monitored quality delta exceeds alert thresholds for N minutes, and immediate fallback to nearest safe profile (e.g., FP16 or higher-precision INT8 variant).
6) Catalog UI/API changes: add 'recommended_profile' and 'quant_guardrails' fields visible in model catalog; expose calibration artifacts link and a 'quant_status' with values [untouched, candidate, signed_off, blocked, rolled_back].

Design notes / Decisions: 
- Use deterministic calibration seeds + fixed dataset slices to ensure reproducible artifacts.
- Keep selector logic rule-based initially (thresholds + simple heuristics) to avoid coupling to model performance predictors; we can iterate toward a learned ranker after collecting historical outcomes.
- Support both FP8 and INT8 variants where hardware supports them; treat FP8 as higher-risk by default and require stricter guardrails (e.g., smaller allowed perplexity change, extra embedding tests).
- Store calibration artifacts in customer-isolated buckets when generated for Dedicated/Private customers; metadata only in catalog for hosted models.

Telemetry & Monitoring: 
- Per-deployment quality delta metrics: task-specific evaluation metric, embedding cosine mean & tail quantiles, token-level perplexity, and a composite "quality_score".
- Cost/latency delta and throughput metrics (p50/p95/p99).
- Alerts: fire when composite quality_score drops >1.5% for 10+ minutes during canary; immediate alert for customer-reported regressions.

Operational playbook:
- Candidate profiles flow: candidate -> signed_off (manual) -> canary -> graduated OR rolled_back.
- In rollback, system should switch traffic gradually to fallback profile but also surface a 'rollback reason' in the catalog history.

Implementation Plan (high level):
Week 1: implement calibration harness skeleton, define canonical calibration dataset slices and seeds.
Week 2: implement selector rule engine and catalog metadata schema changes, wire in artifact links.
Week 3: run calibration across 10 representative models (2 embedding models, 6 decoder LMs, 2 encoder-decoder) and collect reports.
Week 4: integrate canary rollout path + monitoring/alerting, run internal signoff and post-canary evaluation.

Risks & Mitigations: 
- Risk: Calibration dataset mismatch causes unexpected user-facing regressions. Mitigate: include per-model customer usage fingerprint in artifacts and require larger canary windows for models with diverse usage.
- Risk: Overfitting calibration to narrow slices. Mitigate: require cross-slice performance checks and incorporate tail-case tests.

Compliance & Security: Ensure calibration artifacts for Private deployments are uploaded to customer-owned storage and that signer metadata is auditable. Security review required for artifact storage and RBAC for signoff actions.

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the selector + signoff workflow. Separate tickets will cover: 1) kernel/runtime packaging for FP8 on new hardware, 2) learned quant ranking model, and 3) per-customer RBAC for signoff on Private installs.
acceptance_criteria: Selector can generate recommended_profile and fallback_chain metadata for a seeded set of models
Calibration harness produces reproducible artifacts and a human-readable report for each run
Defined numeric guardrails exist and are enforced by the selector (e.g., embedding cosine >= 0.985, perplexity ratio <= 1.03)
Signoff artifact format accepted by catalog ingestion and requires at least one ML engineer + PM signoff
Canary rollout works end-to-end with automatic rollback when quality delta > configured threshold
Model catalog UI shows quant_status and links to calibration artifacts
